Resolves #18829

🌿 *The addon asked Google for the one signal that means "ready" and threw it away. After this, "the addon is ready" and "the API exists" stop being two different claims.*

The Maps wrapper produced no map at all. Opening the example gave a blank area and `ReferenceError: google is not defined`, independent of any API key — the same failure occurs with a valid key, an expired key and no key.

Evidence: L3 (headed browser run of the real example, plus four offline unit arms and a mutation run against `dev`) → L3 required (AC-1 and AC-3 are runtime observations). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered + outside-CI. `test/playwright/unit/main/addon/GoogleMapsReadiness.spec.mjs` asserts readiness at the call boundary; **mutation-verified**, see Test Evidence. In the browser, the example now builds a real map: `mapsCreated: 1`, `Object.values(addon.maps)[0] instanceof google.maps.Map === true`, `markersTotal: 1`, and no `ReferenceError`. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the spec is the first coverage this addon has ever had — `test/` referenced `GoogleMaps` nowhere before. 3 of its 4 arms fail against `dev`. |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: with the key absent the console carries Google's `InvalidKeyMapError` **and** one Neo warning naming `Neo.config.googleMapsApiKey`, and no `ReferenceError`. The warning is visible in the spec's own run output. |
| AC-4 | `git diff origin/dev -- src/main/DomAccess.mjs` is empty. The vendor special-case stayed in the addon that knows about it. |
| AC-5 | outside-CI: the loader pointed at an unroutable host **rejected in 68 ms** with the callback cleaned up, against a 15 s hang detector. Also arm 3 of the spec. |

## Deltas from ticket

**The ticket named one cause and there were two — the second is the real root, and the first was hiding it.**

The ticket prescribed fixing `loadFiles()`. I did, verified the callback fired and `google.maps` was populated, and **the `ReferenceError` persisted**. `RemoteMethodAccess` caches a remote call only when the method is listed in `interceptRemotes`:

```javascript
if (!pkg.isReady && pkg.interceptRemotes?.includes(msg.remoteMethod)) {
    out = pkg.onInterceptRemotes(msg);
```

`GoogleMaps` declared none, so `create()` executed immediately whatever `isReady` said. Both halves are required: without the interception list a correct `loadFiles()` still leaves `create` unguarded, and without the `loadFiles()` fix `isReady` turns true too early and the flushed calls run against an empty global anyway.

`Neo.main.addon.OpenStreetMaps` — same `remote.app` list, same shape — declares `interceptRemotes: ['create']`. **I did not simply copy it.** Its `geocode` is an unimplemented stub, so it is *silent* on that method rather than endorsing its exclusion; Google's `geocode` builds a `new google.maps.Geocoder()` on entry with no map to wait for, so this declares `['create', 'geocode']`. `addMarker` names `google.maps.Marker` too but only inside its `mapCreated` branch, so it already waits.

**Also in scope, small:** the URL literal carried a stray leading space, and gains `loading=async` — which is what Google's console warning asked for and only becomes correct once the callback is honoured.

### A guard I added and then reverted, net −57 lines

`fdf5ad913a` parked the API load on `globalThis` under a `Symbol.for` key so a second addon instance could not steal the single bootstrap callback and leave the first waiting forever. `4de5ba90ba` took it back out after @tobiu falsified the premise: `mainThreadAddons` in `neo-config.json` is one list, and nobody adds a default and a custom addon with the same namespace to it.

**The precise claim, because "fictional" overstated it and @neo-opus-grace was right to say so:** a second instance *is* reachable in principle — `Main#registerAddon` keys its guard on `className` and a `WS/` name resolves to a different module — but reachable in principle is not worth 57 lines. Nothing in this repository pairs an engine addon with a `WS/` twin, and even the pathological `['GoogleMaps', 'WS/GoogleMaps']` collapses to one instance. The surviving docblock records this as a likelihood judgment rather than an impossibility, and names the silent-hang symptom, so anyone who does write that config finds the thread.

The failure mode worth naming: **the risk was one my own fix had created** — on `dev` nothing could hang because nothing waited — and I reached for machinery to offset it instead of first checking whether the scenario was reachable. That check was two greps.

The revert also sharpened the completeness arm. Its regex was `\bgoogle\.`, which matched `loadFiles` through `developers.google.com` in that method's own warning URL — a URL, dereferencing nothing. The false positive had already bought itself an exemption entry whose stated reason the revert made untrue. Now `\bgoogle\.maps\b`, with `addMarker` the only exemption.

## Test Evidence

**Mutation run — the arms restored to `dev`'s `loadFiles()` and config:**

| arm | against `dev` | against this head |
|---|---|---|
| loadFiles does not settle when only the bootstrap script has loaded | **fail** | pass |
| loadFiles hands the API a callback name it actually installed | **fail** | pass |
| a failed script request rejects rather than hanging | pass | pass |
| every method dereferencing the google global is interceptible | **fail** | pass |

`3 failed, 1 passed` on `dev`; `4 passed` here. **The third arm passes on `dev` as well, and that is deliberate rather than a weak arm** — `dev` already rejected on a failed `loadScript`, so that arm guards this rewrite against *losing* the rejection path. Calling it a regression catcher would be false.

The interception arm asserts on the **instance**, not the static class config: `RemoteMethodAccess` reads `pkg.interceptRemotes` where `pkg` is what `Main` instantiated, so a class-level assertion would pass on a class whose instances no longer carry the list.

No arm touches the network — the bootstrap is simulated by resolving a stubbed `loadScript` and then invoking the global the addon registered, which is exactly the ordering the live API produces.

**Browser receipt**, on the real example after the fix:

```
addonIsReady: true · interceptRemotes: ["create","geocode"] · mapsCreated: 1
mapIsRealGoogleMap: true · markersTotal: 1 · callbackCleanedUp: true
```

Remaining console output there is `BillingNotEnabledMapError` (this branch still carries the dead demo key; #18828 replaces it) and the `google.maps.Marker` deprecation, which is out of scope and noted below.

### What the completeness arm does NOT cover

Raised by @neo-opus-grace, recorded here rather than left implicit. The probe matches the literal token `google.maps` in a method's source, so it is blind to a method reaching the global another way — `globalThis.google`, or destructuring `const {maps} = google` first. Every method in the addon today uses the literal form, so the arm is complete **for the current source** and would stay silent on a future method written differently.

Not pushed as a source comment: the arm is at the head @neo-opus-grace approved, and moving it for a comment would cost that seat over documentation. The failure message already prints the found set, which is what makes the gap legible when someone hits it.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] None. Everything here is observable before merge.

## Out of scope, noted

`addMarker` uses `google.maps.Marker`, deprecated since 2024-02-21 in favour of `AdvancedMarkerElement`. Real, unrelated to this race, and recorded under Out of Scope on #18829 — worth its own ticket rather than widening this one.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-17T19:37:22Z

**RA-1 addressed at `fdf5ad913a` — plus a defect of mine that @tobiu's note surfaced, which is the bigger half of this push.**

## RA-1 — you are right, and the derived arm immediately earned itself

The arm claimed the class and asserted two names. It now derives the set from the prototype:

```javascript
Object.getOwnPropertyNames(prototype).filter(name => {
    const {value} = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(prototype, name);
    return name !== 'constructor' && typeof value === 'function' && /\bgoogle\./.test(String(value))
})
```

Descriptors rather than properties, because Neo backs configs with accessors and reading one off a bare prototype runs engine machinery that throws — your `prototype[name]` sketch reds on `getConfig`.

**It found a third method on the first run: `loadFiles`.** Exempt, and for a reason worth stating — it cannot wait for readiness because it *causes* readiness; intercepting it would deadlock. The probe matches it on its own `google.maps` early-out, which is a guard, not a dereference on entry. Two exemptions are now named with reasons, so a future method cannot join them silently. The hardcoded version could not have seen it.

Mutation: dropping `geocode` from `interceptRemotes` reds the arm.

## The defect I introduced, and your non-blocking note was circling it

@tobiu pointed out that addons are exported as classes for extensibility — a user adding logic to one — and that `WS/` addresses a neo workspace's own `src/main/addon/`, the tree `npx neo-app` scaffolds.

That makes a second Maps instance reachable, and **my previous commit turned that into a permanent hang.** The bootstrap calls its callback once per window; I made `loadFiles()` wait for it without making the load shared. A second caller overwrites the first's global, the single callback releases only the later one, and the earlier waits forever with `isReady` false and its intercepted calls cached. **On `dev` nothing hung because nothing waited — I created this by adding the wait.**

The load now lives on `globalThis` under `Symbol.for('neo.main.addon.GoogleMaps.apiLoad')` rather than in module scope: the resource belongs to the window, and a renamed workspace copy is a *different module* with its own scope, so module scope could not have shared it. A registered symbol is the one slot both resolve to. Plus an early return when `google.maps` is already live, and a rejected load clears the slot so a failure does not become the permanent answer.

Mutation: reverting to a per-call promise reds the new second-instance arm.

**Your non-blocking hypothesis is the same family and still stands.** A stub that downloads and never calls back still leaves the addon quietly not-ready. Sharing the load removes the cause I introduced; it does not add a timeout. I would rather ship a timeout with a measured duration than a guessed one, so I am leaving it as a separate concern rather than folding a magic number into this PR — say if you would rather it landed here.

Six arms now, `6 passed`. Browser receipt unchanged: `isReady: true`, one real `google.maps.Map`, one marker, no `ReferenceError`.

## What ships

Two causes, both load-bearing. `loadFiles()` now awaits the bootstrap's `callback` rather than the script's `load` event, and `interceptRemotes: ['create', 'geocode']` keeps the methods that dereference `google` on entry from running before the API exists. Either alone leaves the example broken.

Four unit arms, first coverage this addon has ever had. Three red against `dev`; the fourth guards the rejection path `dev` already had.

## Two corrections of yours are in the diff

- **Addons are instantiated by `Main`**, so the interception arm asserts on a real instance rather than the static class config — `RemoteMethodAccess` reads `pkg.interceptRemotes` off what `registerAddon` created.
- **`neo-config.json` cannot express two Maps addons**, so the 57 lines I had added to guard a second-instance hang are reverted. @neo-opus-grace's refinement is in the body: reachable *in principle* is not the same as fictional, and the surviving docblock records it as a likelihood judgment that names the symptom, rather than claiming impossibility.

## Not blocking, recorded rather than absorbed

The completeness arm matches the literal token `google.maps`, so a future method reaching the global as `globalThis.google`, or destructuring `maps` first, would stay invisible to it. Complete for today's source, not for every way the global can be spelled. @neo-opus-grace raised it; it is in the body under Test Evidence rather than as a source comment, because moving the head for a comment would have cost her approval.

## Sequencing with #18828

Independent diffs, but #18828's AC-2 rides on this one: until this merges, a reader with a placeholder key sees a blank area and a `ReferenceError` instead of Google's own *"Oops! Something went wrong"* panel. Either order merges cleanly; this one first is what makes #18828 fully true.
